choices.term: Ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ' αὐτῷ, οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ. Παυσάτω τὴν γλῶσσαν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ κακοῦ.
choices.english: two separate items: the end of the note on 1 Peter 2:6, then the lemma of 1 Peter 3:10
choices.why: The old English joined the 1 Peter 2:6 line to the next note with 'because', inventing a link. The Greek ends one note and prints a new lemma (1 Peter 3:10), on which Cyril's next note comments; James 3:2 is quoted inside that note.
rejected: The one believing in him will not be put to shame, because it is essential to control one's tongue

choices.term: Γέγραπται γὰρ ... Ἔφη δέ που καὶ ὁ Χριστοῦ μαθητής
choices.english: For it is written ... And the disciple of Christ also said somewhere
choices.why: Kept as Cyril's own citations; the old English replaced them with 'as the Bible says' and 'a crucial aspect of being a perfect person'.
rejected: a crucial aspect of being a perfect person

choices.term: Ἐν ᾧ καὶ τοῖς ἐν φυλάκῃ πνεύμασι ... (1 Peter 3:19-20) and Λύει ἐνταῦθα τὴν ἀντίθεσιν
choices.english: lemma and the opening of Cyril's note, translated
choices.why: The old English dropped the lemma and the objection ('why did he not become man many ages earlier?') and moved later sentences forward.

choices.term: Τουτέστι, καὶ τοῖς ἐν ᾅδου ἐκήρυξεν ...
choices.english: That is, he also preached to those in Hades ...
choices.why: This repeats the sense of the earlier sentence, but it is joined to the running text by 'That is' with no tag or page mark, and it differs in wording ('in the time of their life'); treated as the author's restatement, not a second catena form, so it is kept.

choices.term: ἵνα καὶ πιστῶς ἐπιγνοῖεν ... ἵνα ... ἔχοιεν αἰτιᾶσθαι
choices.english: had no strength to look ... so as to recognize in faith ...; so those who fell away ... would have themselves to blame
choices.why: The first ἵνα gives what blindness prevented; the second gives the purpose of the open proclamation. The old English said the souls 'could not faithfully recognize' and dropped the second clause.
rejected: and thus they could not faithfully recognize the one who came to free all

The one believing on him will not be put to shame. [Lemma, 1 Peter 3:10:] Let him stop his tongue from evil. [Catena tag: Of Cyril.] Befitting saints is the lesson and saving, and I say that the guidance is worthy of every word (attention). For it is written that Death and life [are] in the hand of the tongue; and those who rule it will eat its fruits. And somewhere the disciple of Christ also said: If anyone does not stumble in word, this one is a perfect man, able to bridle also the whole body. Great therefore is the self-control of the tongue, just as, surely, not being so is a most grievous disease. [Lemma, 1 Peter 3:19-20:] In which also, having gone, he preached to the spirits in prison, who once disobeyed, when the patience of God was waiting, in the days of Noah, the ark being prepared, into which few, that is eight, souls were saved through water. [Catena tag: Of Cyril.] He resolves here that objection which some, objecting, say: If the becoming-man is beneficial, why ever did he not become man many ages before? For behold, also to the spirits in prison, having gone, he preached, so that he might loose these, as many as were going to believe, if at that point of time, having become flesh, he had visited those on earth. For these surely recognized him also appearing in the [places] under the earth, and enjoyed the appearing. Having gone with the soul, he preached to those in Hades, as a soul seen with souls; whom the gatekeepers of Hades, seeing, cowered, and bronze gates were crushed, and iron bars were broken; and the Only-begotten was calling with authority to the souls of like passions, according to the principle of the economy, saying to those in bonds: Go out [manuscript: Go out, other form], and to those in the darkness: [page number 8, not translated] Be uncovered. For the greater part of the economy [wrought] for us is beyond nature and tradition [column number 74.1016, not translated]; so just as Christ called out to all those on earth with equal honor through the presence in flesh, and those who believed were benefited, so also through the descent into Hades he freed from the bonds of death those believing and having recognized him. pass_b_english: …freedom. He says, “I lay the chosen stone in the foundations of Zion” (Isaiah 28:16). And what good comes of it? “Whoever believes in him will never be put to shame.”
“Let him keep his tongue from evil” (1 Peter 3:10).

From Cyril: The lesson is worthy of the saints and brings salvation, and I say the instruction deserves every attention. For it is written, “Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who master it will eat its fruits” (Proverbs 18:21). And the disciple of Christ also said somewhere, “If anyone does not stumble in word, he is a perfect man, able to bridle the whole body as well” (James 3:2). Great, then, is mastery of the tongue, just as, of course, not having it is a most grievous disease.

“In which he also went and preached to the spirits in prison, who had once disobeyed, when God’s patience waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was being built, in which a few, that is, eight souls, were brought safely through water” (1 Peter 3:19–20).

From Cyril: Here he answers the objection that some raise when they say, “If the incarnation is beneficial, why did he not become man many ages earlier?” For see: he went and preached even to the spirits in prison, to set free all of them who would have believed if he had taken flesh at that time and come among those on the earth. For these surely recognized him when he appeared even in the regions under the earth, and they enjoyed his appearing.

Going in his soul, he preached to those in Hades, seen as a soul among souls. When the gatekeepers of Hades saw him, they cowered (Job 38:17); gates of bronze were shattered and bars of iron were crushed (Psalm 107:16). And the Only-begotten called with authority to the souls who shared his condition, in keeping with the plan of salvation, saying to those in bonds, “Come out,” and to those in darkness, “Be uncovered” (Isaiah 49:9).

That is, he also preached to those in Hades, to set free all of them who would have believed if he had taken flesh and come to live among them in the time of their life; for these surely recognized him, even in Hades. For most of the plan carried out for us is beyond nature and beyond tradition. So, just as Christ, by his presence in the flesh, called out to all on earth on equal terms, and those who believed were helped, so too by his descent into Hades he set free from the bonds of death those who believed and recognized him. For the souls of those who had lived in idolatry and lawless debauchery, blinded, as it were, by their attachment to the flesh, had no strength to look toward the rays of the divine appearing, so as to recognize in faith the one who, to set all free (as far as it rested with him), appeared to those under the earth, preached to all alike, and showed justice together with his love for humankind.
